title: Property or Mutual Funds: Where Should NRIs Invest in India?
description: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) have distinct rules for investing in India, making the choice between property and mutual funds complex. Real estate offers tangib.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in any property in India?
faq.a: No, NRIs cannot acquire agricultural land, plantation property, or farmhouses in India. They are permitted to purchase residential or commercial properties.

faq.q: What are the tax implications for NRIs on rental income from Indian property?
faq.a: Rental income earned by NRIs from property in India is taxable at applicable slab rates. A standard deduction of 30% is allowed, and interest on housing loans can also be deducted.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how much an NRI can repatriate from India?
faq.a: Repatriation from an NRO account is limited to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to tax clearances. Funds from NRE accounts are generally fully repatriable.

faq.q: Do NRIs need a PAN card to invest in Indian mutual funds?
faq.a: Yes, a Permanent Account Number (PAN) card is mandatory for NRIs to complete their Know Your Customer (KYC) process and invest in Indian mutual funds.

faq.q: How are long-term capital gains from equity mutual funds taxed for NRIs?
faq.a: Long-term capital gains (LTCG) from equity mutual funds are taxed at 10% for gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year, without indexation benefit.

faq.q: What are NRE and NRO accounts used for?
faq.a: NRE accounts are for depositing foreign earnings and are fully repatriable, with tax-exempt interest. NRO accounts are for managing income earned in India, and while principal from foreign sources can be repatriated, interest and Indian-sourced income are taxable.
